description: Unveiling hidden seismicity: An AI-derived catalog of 380k earthquakes for Sichuan Province, China is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ting Yang et al. Long-term, high-resolution seismic monitoring is a prerequisite for characterizing seismic structures, delineating fault geometry, and mitigating earthquake risks. Located on the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, Sichuan Province is among the most seismically active regions in China, with particularly intense activity concentrated in the shale gas extraction zones of the southern Sichuan Basin. Coverage: national (CN); published in 2026. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
